summary: Count out loud by ones to 20.
Know and name the written numbers 0 to 10.
Know that zero means there is nothing to count.
Count up to 10 objects set out in a row or a column and say how many.
Count objects one by one, one number each, and match groups up to 10.
Know the last number said when counting tells how many in all, up to 10.
Count up to 5 things scattered about, not lined up.
Compare two groups of 0 to 5: say which has more, fewer or the same.
Sort up to 5 objects by color, size or shape, and say what they share.
Spot, copy and continue repeating patterns with objects, sounds or moves.
Point to a circle, square, rectangle or triangle when it's named.
Describe what can be measured with words like big, long, short, tall, heavy.
Compare two objects directly: longer or shorter, heavier or lighter, taller.
Sort objects into groups by one or more features.
Gather and organize information about things and events around them.
Make a graph with real objects from sorted groups, with a grown-up's help.
